history.summary: IDENTITY FLAG: 'Ramakrishna Temple, Purulia' has no exact standalone record; it is documented here as the main shrine/prayer hall of the Ramakrishna Mission Vidyapith, the well-known Ramakrishna Mission centre in Purulia district (verify if the CSV intends a different, smaller temple). CSV TOWN FLAG: the temple is on the Vidyapith campus at Bongabari/Vivekananda Nagar (Purulia-II), ~10 km from Purulia town, not in Purulia town itself. The Vidyapith was founded in 1957 by Swami Hiranmayananda at the invitation of West Bengal chief minister Bidhan Chandra Roy after Purulia's 1956 annexation to West Bengal; the main shrine houses a marble image of Sri Ramakrishna in the garbhagriha and the Holy Trio. The campus runs on the Gurukula system and won the state's Best School Award in 2018.

name: Ramakrishna Temple, Purulia
town_description: Purulia is the district headquarters of Purulia district in southwestern West Bengal, a town known for Chhau dance, the Ayodhya Hills, and the Ramakrishna Mission Vidyapith.
